overall_summary: View counts across all 10 videos are extremely low (ranging from 5 to 34 views), indicating an early-stage channel with minimal baseline distribution. However, 'self respect' and boundary-setting topics (like deleting chats or numbers) performed relatively better, showing early signs of audience resonance with empowerment over pure sadness.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos under 'self respect' like AfaLxMy6FMY (34 views) and aNR94Xxn0yM (24 views, 1 like) outperformed generic sadness clips.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on the transition from heartbreak to reclaiming self-worth.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focused purely on waiting or generic night thoughts (e.g., uIbMpCjVutQ, aUuNKfe7jm4) hovered around 5 views.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid passive longing hooks; pair emotional triggers with active emotional decisions.

next_video.concept: A story about muting status updates of someone who still watches yours, realizing your peace matters more than their attention.
next_video.opening_direction: Start with the specific action of seeing their view on your story first, yet they never reply.
next_video.twist_direction: Instead of waiting for their message, you remove them from your viewers list entirely—choosing inner peace over curiosity.
next_video.reason: Previous successful uploads (like AfaLxMy6FMY and aNR94Xxn0yM) performed best when published around midday (13:40 - 13:50 UTC/IST equivalent window).

experiment: Testing an active self-respect boundary (muting/blocking stories) instead of passive chat/number staring to see if empowerment drives higher engagement.
